stories.headline: Global civil-society groups warn China is exporting political red lines abroad
stories.summary: Global Issues/IPS highlights CIVICUS concerns after RightsCon 2026 was cancelled, framing it as part of a broader pattern of transnational repression and pressure on freedom of expression beyond China’s borders.
stories.pastoral_note: Pray for believers and neighbours who live under coercive power. This is a reminder that the church’s witness includes telling the truth without fear and protecting space for conscience, speech, and worship.

stories.headline: Christian teacher beheaded after school attacks in Nigeria
stories.summary: International Christian Concern reports that Michael Oyedokun, a Christian math teacher in Oyo state, Nigeria, was abducted and killed after armed men attacked several schools near Ogbomoso.
stories.pastoral_note: Hold Nigeria before the Lord by name today. This is not abstract suffering; it is a teacher, a family, students, and a local church grieving under the cross and waiting for resurrection hope.

stories.headline: Many churchgoers still do not see spiritual matters as part of everyday conversation
stories.summary: Lifeway Research says a new May 19 report finds that although living unashamed is a marker of discipleship, many churchgoers do not view spiritual matters as pervasive across daily life and conversation.
stories.pastoral_note: This names a discipleship gap worth preaching into: faith is not merely private belief but allegiance expressed in ordinary speech, work, friendship, and dependence on Jesus.

stories.headline: Christianity Today asks whether agentic AI will make people more restless, not more rested
stories.summary: A Christianity Today essay argues that autonomous AI agents may complete projects with less human prompting, but time-saving technology cannot heal hurry, discontentment, or a disordered relationship with Sabbath.
stories.pastoral_note: A timely discipleship angle: tools can multiply output, but only worship can reorder desire. Sabbath remains a sign that we are creatures beloved by God, not machines justified by productivity.

stories.headline: HBR explores whether leaders should treat AI like a teammate
stories.summary: Harvard Business Review’s May leadership page features Gretchen Gavett’s “Should You Treat AI Like a Teammate?”, connecting AI agents with automation, motivation, management, and leadership practices.
stories.pastoral_note: For church teams, the question is not only efficiency but formation: what work should be delegated, what judgment must remain human, and how do leaders preserve trust, clarity, and care?

stories.headline: Fraser Valley sales rise, but conditions remain in buyers’ favour
stories.summary: The Fraser Valley Real Estate Board reported 1,118 MLS sales in April, up 11% from March and 7% year over year, while active listings reached 9,816, about 45% above the 10-year seasonal average.
stories.pastoral_note: Housing pressure remains a pastoral reality in the Lower Mainland. Behind every market statistic are young families, renters, seniors, and newcomers trying to discern stability and calling.

stories.headline: DailyGood marks 29 years of curating stories that nurture the heart
stories.summary: DailyGood’s May 21 page describes its long-running work of sharing uplifting stories that connect hearts and inspire action, reaching more than 139,000 subscribers without ads or agenda-driven appeals.
stories.pastoral_note: In a news cycle trained for alarm, deliberately noticing goodness is spiritual resistance. Philippians 4 still matters: whatever is lovely, commendable, excellent, or praiseworthy—think on these things.

stories.headline: Canadian coverage notes Gen Z interest in faith is becoming publicly visible
stories.summary: CTV’s feature on a return to faith reports religious leaders saying Gen Z is helping reverse decades of religious decline, even as the broader picture remains complex and uneven.
stories.pastoral_note: This is an evangelistic doorway, not a victory lap. Young people are not looking for slick religion; they are hungry for reality, belonging, holiness, and a gospel embodied by credible adults.
